chunks: A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Khalid, from Abdullah ibn Muhammad al-Nahiki, from Ammar ibn Marwan al-Qandi, from Abdullah ibn Sinan, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:
There is no small (sin) with persistence (upon it), and there is no major (sin) with seeking forgiveness.
ai.seo_question: How does persistence or forgiveness change the weight of a sin in Shia Islam?
ai.summary: This concise hadith from Imam al-Sadiq (AS) highlights the dynamic nature of sin's weight based on the sinner's attitude, a concept central to Shia ethical jurisprudence. It underscores that persistence (istishab) transforms minor sins into major ones by hardening the heart, while sincere repentance (istighfar) can elevate the status of major sins by demonstrating humility and reliance on Divine mercy. This principle serves as a crucial motivational tool for believers, balancing the fear of escalating minor transgressions with the hope of forgiveness for grave errors.

en.hubeali:
A number of our companions, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad Bin Khalid, from Abdullah Bin Muhammad Al Naheyki, from Ammar Bin Marwan Al Qandy, from Abdullah Bin Sinan, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said:
‘There is neither a small (sin) along with the persistence (upon it), nor is there a major (sin) along with the (seeking of) Forgiveness’.
en.sarwar: 1. A number of our people have narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Khalid from ‘Abd Allah ibn Muhammad al-Nuhayki from ‘Ammar ibn Marwan al- Qandi from ‘Abd Allah ibn Sinan from abu ‘Abd Allah (a.s.) who has said the following: “
Minor sins are not minor if one persists committing such sins and major sins are not major if followed by plea for forgiveness.”
